launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.address: 5700 North Eagle Creek Parkway, Indianapolis, IN 46254
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.summary: A 5,300-acre reservoir and forest park with two nature centers, a swimming beach, marina, trails, birding, playgrounds, picnic areas and a canine companion zone.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.hours: Gate hours vary by month: 7:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. in December and January; 7:00 a.m.-6:30 p.m. in November and February; 7:00 a.m.-7:30 p.m. in October and March; 7:00 a.m.-8:30 p.m. in September and April; 7:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. in May; and 7:00 a.m.-9:30 p.m. June through August.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.parking: Vehicle admission includes use of park parking. Enter at 5700 North Eagle Creek Parkway from 56th Street or 7100 North Eagle Creek Parkway from 71st Street, then follow the official park map to the selected facility; the two entrances do not provide equally short approaches to every destination.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.arrival: Choose the destination before entering. The 56th Street entrance is the practical approach for many southern and central facilities, while the 71st Street entrance is closer to the northern nature-center and birding area.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.restrooms: The official map identifies restrooms at developed facilities and picnic areas, with the nature centers providing the most reliable staffed access during their shorter building hours. Remote trails and shoreline areas should not be assumed to have nearby facilities.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.cost: Day admission is $6 per resident vehicle, $8 per nonresident vehicle, $1 per hiker or bicyclist, and $15 per bus. A car-top boat launch is $3 per vessel plus vehicle admission; rentals, reservations, dog-zone access and commercial attractions can cost extra.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.accessibility: The two nature centers and major developed facilities have paved approaches, but wooded trails, shorelines and older recreation areas vary. Indy Parks reports an active accessibility-upgrade project for Pin Oak Trail; verify the route needed before relying on unfinished improvements.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.dogs: Dogs must remain leashed except inside the Canine Companion Zone. Keep pets away from the swimming beach and wildlife-sensitive areas where posted, and carry out waste.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.family: The nature centers, playgrounds and seasonal beach support very different visits. Confirm center hours, lifeguard presence and weather-dependent operations before promising a particular activity.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.transit: The 2026 IndyGo system map shows service near the 56th Street corridor, but the park is large and internal destinations are widely separated. Check the trip planner for the chosen entrance and expect substantial walking if arriving without a car.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.need: Swim only when lifeguards are present. Bicycles are limited to roadways, boats must follow horsepower and launch rules, and the waterfowl sanctuary prohibits watercraft. Do not leave valuables in vehicles.
launch-in-indianapolis-eagle-creek-park.weather: Check National Weather Service Indianapolis forecasts and current Indy Parks notices. Heat, thunderstorms, high wind, ice, snow, reservoir conditions and flooding can independently affect trails, boating, swimming, nature centers and gates.

launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.address: Monon Trail at East 10th Street, Indianapolis, IN 46202
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.summary: Indianapolis's north-south rail trail, running from 10th Street to 96th Street before continuing into Hamilton County and connecting with major greenways, parks and neighborhoods.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.hours: The Monon Trail page does not publish a separate schedule. Indy Parks' system rules state that park hours are dawn to dusk; posted closures, construction and connected-park hours can supersede that general rule.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.parking: There is no single trail parking lot. Choose a legal access point before driving; the operator identifies connections at parks including Frank and Judy O'Bannon Park, Canterbury Park and Marott Park, but each location has its own parking and construction conditions.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.arrival: The Indianapolis segment runs from near East 10th Street to 96th Street. Choose a neighborhood or connection first—downtown/10th Street, Fall Creek, the State Fairgrounds, Canterbury, Broad Ripple or Marott Woods—rather than navigating to one generic midpoint.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.restrooms: The operator does not list trailwide restrooms. Comfort stations or indoor facilities may be available at selected connected parks and businesses, but hours and access vary; do not plan a long trip around an assumed facility.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.cost: Indy Parks lists no admission fee for ordinary Monon Trail use. Parking, transit, food, events and separately operated attractions may charge.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.accessibility: Use the official trail map to choose an access point and review street crossings. The operator does not publish a trailwide accessibility guarantee, and curb cuts, construction, detours and connected-park surfaces can vary by segment.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.dogs: Indy Parks requires dogs to remain on a leash shorter than 20 feet outside designated dog parks. Keep animals controlled around bicycles, runners, crossings and crowded Broad Ripple segments, and remove waste.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.family: The trail can support short family rides and walks, but it is a shared transportation corridor with street crossings and faster users. Choose a short segment near a connected park and supervise children closely.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.transit: IndyGo's 2026 system map shows multiple routes crossing or approaching the Monon, including service around 10th Street, the State Fairgrounds, Broad Ripple and 86th Street. Check the current route page for the selected access point.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.need: The trail connects with Fall Creek Greenway, Central Canal Towpath and the White River trail network. Construction at Canterbury Park is expected through late 2026, so verify current detours and avoid treating every adjacent park as an open trailhead.
launch-in-indianapolis-monon-trail.weather: Check National Weather Service Indianapolis forecasts before a long trip. Heat, lightning, high wind, heavy rain, snow and ice can make exposed bridges, shaded pavement and street crossings unsafe even when the corridor is not formally closed.
